channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: New Substation and Power Line Built in Romit, Tajikistan for Mountain Villages
item.description: The second phase of the 'Romit Power Grid Construction' project is underway, focusing on building the 'Yavroz' substation and a 10 kV power line to supply electricity to the village of Yos. Construction includes the substation control building and foundations for high-voltage equipment. The power line traverses difficult mountainous terrain.

item.title: Prime Ministers of Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan Hold Official Meeting in Bishkek
item.description: The Prime Ministers of Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, Oljas Bektenov and Adylbek Kasymaliev, held an official meeting at the "Ala-Archa" state residence in Bishkek. The ceremony included a guard of honor and the playing of national anthems. The leaders are scheduled to hold negotiations, participate in the second interregional cooperation forum, and attend the 14th session of the Kyrgyz-Kazakh intergovernmental council.

item.title: International Congress on Pediatric Oncology and Hematology Held in Samarkand
item.description: The second international congress on pediatric oncology and hematology, themed "From Recovery to Improving Quality of Life," took place in Samarkand as part of the "Investing in Children's Well-being" Global Summit. Health ministers from Uzbekistan, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan, along with WHO and SIOP representatives, attended. The congress highlighted progress in Uzbekistan's national strategy and specialized centers.

item.title: Ansar Aidarov Appointed New Chairman of Samruk-Energy
item.description: Ansar Aidarov has been appointed the new Chairman of the Management Board of Samruk-Energy. The decision was made by the Management Board of Samruk-Kazyna. The head of the holding, Nurlan Zhakupov, introduced Aidarov to the team and emphasized the need for strict adherence to investment project timelines and timely commissioning of power plants. Aidarov previously held various positions within the Samruk-Kazyna group.

item.title: Tajikistan President Inaugurates New Autism Center in Dushanbe, Lays Foundation for Transplant Center
item.description: On October 30, President Emomali Rahmon inaugurated a new Autism Center in Dushanbe's Firdausi district and laid the foundation stone for a transplant center. The autism center will provide diagnosis, treatment, rehabilitation, and education for children with various developmental disorders. The transplant center will focus on organ and tissue transplantation and post-operative care.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey to Expand Trade Preferences and Establish Business Support Council
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkey signed five documents in Ankara on October 29, 2026, aimed at expanding trade preferences, facilitating customs information exchange, protecting citizens' social rights, and establishing a High-Level Council for Business Support. The new council will promote trade and investment, with Turkish Vice President Cevdet Yılmaz leading the Turkish side.

item.title: Attempt to smuggle gold worth $500,000 from Shymkent to Turkey foiled
item.description: Approximately 2.8 kilograms of gold, valued at 227.8 million tenge (approximately $500,000), was confiscated in Shymkent, Kazakhstan. Uzbek citizens attempted to illegally transport the gold to Turkey by concealing it within the lining of their luggage. The suspects are now subject to an international manhunt, and pre-trial investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Nearly all Bishkek heating facilities connected to central heating system
item.description: Approximately 97 percent of facilities serviced by Bishkek's municipal heating enterprise 'Bishkekteploenergo' have been connected to the central heating system. As of 10:00 AM, 99 percent of the enterprise's boiler houses were operational. Heating has been supplied to all healthcare facilities, kindergartens, and higher education institutions, along with most schools and residential buildings.

item.title: Head of Samruk-Energo Dismissed Over Unsatisfactory Work Pace
item.description: The head of "Samruk-Energo", Kairat Maksutov, has been dismissed from his position. This decision comes after previous criticism regarding the slow progress of work at the Almaty Thermal Power Plant-3. Maksutov had received a reprimand a year ago and was criticized three months prior for the low pace of work.

item.title: Miner Dies in "QazHrom" Mine in Aktobe Region Following Accident
item.description: A miner has died in the "QazHrom" mine in the Aktobe region after sustaining injuries while coupling wagons. The incident occurred at the mine named after the 10th anniversary of Kazakhstan's Independence. This is the second fatal accident at the company's mines in nine days, following a previous collapse that killed a 24-year-old worker.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Begin Testing Digital Som Platform in 2027
item.description: The National Bank of Kyrgyzstan plans to start testing the digital som platform in 2027. The timeline for its availability to citizens and businesses for daily transactions is not yet determined. The regulator aims to complete the basic version of the platform by the end of 2026, with funding provided by the National Bank's own resources.

item.title: Ansar Aidarov Appointed Head of Samruk-Energy
item.description: Ansar Aidarov has been appointed chairman of the board of Samruk-Energy. The decision was made by the fund's management. The new head was tasked with strictly adhering to investment project timelines and ensuring timely commissioning of power plants. Aidarov previously held positions within the Samruk-Kazyna group.

item.title: US Vice President Vance: Trump Will Not Allow Iran Conflict to Become a 'Forever War'
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance stated that Donald Trump would prevent the conflict with Iran from escalating into a prolonged war. Vance defended the administration's military actions in the Middle East, emphasizing that while the US has been involved with Iran for 47 years, the current military campaign has lasted seven months. He asserted that opposing lengthy wars does not mean rejecting military force.

item.title: Large Oil Exploration Site in Kazakhstan's Ulytau Region Offered for Auction
item.description: A significant oil exploration site in Kazakhstan's Ulytau region, covering over 1,100 square kilometers, has been put up for auction. The winning company will be required to conduct geological exploration and drill at least one exploratory well. Additional obligations will be imposed if substantial oil or gas reserves are discovered. The electronic auction is scheduled for December 23.

item.title: Afghanistan Road Closures Disrupt Markets and Cause Shortages, Report Finds
item.description: Conflict-related road damage and closures affected 39 communities across 28 districts in Afghanistan during late 2025 and the first half of 2026. A report by REACH and WFP indicates these disruptions impacted markets, delayed goods movement, and led to shortages in some areas. Longer closures, especially with limited alternative routes, had the most severe consequences, including population displacement.

item.title: Houthis Claim Missile Strikes on Saudi Oil Refinery and Military Sites
item.description: Yemen's Houthi movement claimed responsibility for missile attacks on Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Defense building in Riyadh, an oil refinery, and military facilities on October 27, 2026. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saria stated ballistic missiles were used, hitting targets including a refinery in Ras Tanura and military sites in Najran and Khamis Mushait. Saudi authorities reported intercepting missiles but confirmed debris caused damage in Riyadh.

item.title: Zero Child Vaccination Rates Recorded in Some Almaty Clinics Amid Measles Outbreak
item.description: Zero vaccination rates for children under 16 have been recorded in some medical facilities in Almaty, Kazakhstan, according to the Ministry of Health. Health Minister Akmaral Alnazarova highlighted these figures during a meeting, noting that target vaccination rates were not met despite a rise in measles cases. The Sanitary and Epidemiological Control Department was tasked with strengthening oversight of immunization requirements.

item.title: Kazakhstan Investors Can Earn Beyond Dollar and Tenge, Expert Says
item.description: Kazakhstan investors can explore earnings beyond the dollar and tenge, according to macroanalyst Nazerke Sadenova of BCC Invest. While the tenge offers higher deposit rates, potential currency depreciation and monetary policy shifts pose risks. Investors should consider euro and Japanese yen as alternatives.

item.title: Stray Dogs Kill Nearly 50 Sheep in Northern Kazakhstan Village
item.description: In the village of Pribrezhny, northern Kazakhstan, stray dogs have attacked sheep, killing nearly 50 and injuring several more. Residents are concerned about the dogs attacking people, especially children, and are demanding authorities address the issue by culling the stray population.

item.title: CIS Antitrust Authorities Discuss AI Impact on Competition and Drug Prices
item.description: CIS antitrust bodies met in Khankendi, Azerbaijan, to discuss the impact of artificial intelligence on competition, drug price regulation, consumer lending, and roaming tariffs. Representatives from Tajikistan, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, and Uzbekistan attended the 47th meeting of the Antitrust Legislation Violations Joint Investigation Headquarters.

item.title: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan Discuss Construction of Kambarata HPP-1
item.description: Representatives from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan met in Istanbul to discuss the next steps for the Kambarata HPP-1 project, a 1860 MW hydroelectric power plant. The project, planned on the Naryn River in Kyrgyzstan, aims to increase Central Asia's energy potential and strengthen regional cooperation in water and energy resources.

item.title: Police in Zhanaozen Stop Illegal Circulation of Oil Products
item.description: Police in Zhanaozen, Mangystau region, have uncovered and stopped the illegal circulation of oil products. During an operation, officers seized four tons of oil products from a private base in the industrial zone. A criminal case has been initiated, and investigations are ongoing to determine the origin of the products and the circumstances of the incident.

item.title: Uzbekistan Increases Income Threshold for Electricity and Gas Compensation
item.description: Uzbekistan has raised the income threshold for receiving compensation for electricity and gas. The income criterion for identifying needy families will now be doubled the minimum subsistence costs. The deadline for compensation payments for electricity and natural gas has been extended to April 1, 2028, and for coal, to January 1, 2029.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allows Individuals Under 18 to Obtain Education Loans
item.description: Kazakhstan now permits individuals under 18 to obtain education loans for tuition fees. These loans are available not only to university students but also to college students and master's candidates. Parental consent is required for applicants under 18. Banks will assess applications based on credit history and income.

item.title: Russia Confirms Balkhash NPP Project on Schedule, Boosting Regional Energy Security
item.description: Russia's Foreign Ministry stated the Balkhash Nuclear Power Plant project in Kazakhstan is proceeding on schedule, with construction set to begin in 2027. The plant is crucial for Kazakhstan's energy balance until 2035 and will enhance Central Asia's energy security. Rosatom leads the international consortium, with two VVER-1200 units planned for completion by 2035-2036.

item.title: Almaty Reports 13.5% of Cars Exceeded Emission Standards in September LEZ Monitoring
item.description: In September, 13.5% of vehicles checked within Almaty's low-emission zone (LEZ) exceeded harmful emission standards, according to the city administration. Out of 6,833 vehicles monitored, 922 showed elevated levels. More than half of these vehicles passed subsequent tests after fuel system adjustments.

item.title: Almaty Medical Workers Report Sanitary Norm Violations at RFMSH School
item.description: Medical workers in Almaty have reported violations of sanitary norms at the RFMSH school. The specific details of the reported violations were not provided in the source text, but the report indicates a concern regarding the school's adherence to health and safety standards.

item.title: Illegal Oil Products Trade Disrupted in Zhanaozen, Criminal Case Opened
item.description: Police in Mangystau region have uncovered an alleged illegal trade of oil products in Zhanaozen. Law enforcement officers detained a man on a private base in the industrial zone and seized a four-ton container of petroleum products. A criminal case has been initiated, and authorities are working to determine the origin of the products and all circumstances of the incident.

item.title: Taliban Report Over 100 Migrant Families Forcibly Returned to Afghanistan
item.description: The Taliban announced the forced return of 150 migrant families, totaling 709 people, to Afghanistan. Hamdullah Fitrat, deputy spokesperson for the Taliban, stated that families returned through various border crossings, including Torkham in Nangarhar, Spin Boldak in Kandahar, Pul-e Abrisham in Nimruz, and Islam Qala in Herat provinces.

item.title: Bacteria Found at Almaty School After Mass Student Food Poisoning Incident
item.description: An inspection of a school in Almaty revealed coliform bacteria in food samples and on dishes following a mass food poisoning incident. Four cafeteria workers were found to be carriers of Staphylococcus aureus. Violations of food storage, documentation, and equipment sanitation were also noted.

item.title: Azerbaijan's President Aliyev to Skip Summit Amidst Hijab Dispute with Turkey
item.description: Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev will not attend the Turkic States Organization summit in Ankara due to a "pre-planned event" and a "tight work schedule." This comes amid an open dispute between Ankara and Baku over Azerbaijan's restrictions on wearing the hijab in schools. Turkey has urged Azerbaijan to reconsider the ban.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Constitutional Court Clarifies Housing Payment Regulations
item.description: The Constitutional Court of the Republic of Kazakhstan has issued clarifications regarding the number of housing payments. The ruling addresses specific questions concerning the application of housing benefits.

item.title: Kazakhstan Police Widows Demand Fair Payments Amidst Benefit Disputes
item.description: Widows of deceased Kazakh police officers are protesting reduced payments and demands to return funds, which they claim were wrongly classified as overpayments. One widow, whose husband died in 2020, highlighted the struggle for fair benefits, with legal battles and recent payment issues causing distress.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Install Smart Video Surveillance Systems at Reservoirs
item.description: Uzbekistan will implement AI-powered smart video surveillance systems at reservoirs and adjacent tourist areas to enhance safety and digitalize operations. These systems will detect drowning risks and unauthorized access in real-time, automatically alerting rescue services.

item.title: Uzbek Citizens Detained Attempting to Illegally Smuggle Gold to Turkey
item.description: Two Uzbek citizens were apprehended at Shymkent Airport attempting to illegally smuggle approximately 2.8 kilograms of gold, valued at 227.8 million tenge, to Turkey. The gold was confiscated in favor of the state. Investigations are ongoing, and international wanted notices have been issued for the suspects.

item.title: Expert: Kazakhstan needs to use its resources more effectively to reach high-income status
item.description: An expert stated that middle-income countries must more effectively utilize human capital and other resources to transition to high-income status. He noted that countries like Kazakhstan differ from high-income nations in the efficiency of resource utilization. The experience of Argentina, Brazil, and Mexico shows the difficulty of overcoming this economic development stage.

item.title: St. Petersburg bans migrants from working in shops, salons, and sports facilities
item.description: Authorities in St. Petersburg, Russia, have prohibited migrants holding work permits from working in specific sectors. The ban affects jobs in retail, hairdressing salons, beauty parlors, and sports facilities. This measure restricts employment opportunities for foreign workers in these areas.

item.title: Binance Reports $6.3 Billion Lost in Cryptocurrency Exchange Security Breach
item.description: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, announced a security breach resulting in losses estimated at $6.3 billion. The exchange stated that with partner assistance, approximately $3 billion in affected assets have been restricted. Binance has committed to covering all losses and is cooperating with law enforcement to track and recover the funds, assuring users their funds remain secure.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Offer Land Around Reservoirs for Tourism Development via Auction
item.description: Uzbekistan has adopted a presidential decree to develop tourism and economic potential around reservoirs. Vacant non-agricultural lands near reservoirs in ten regions will be offered for tourism services through an electronic auction. Funds raised will be used for infrastructure development, considering natural disaster risks.

item.title: Afghanistan: Phase One of Kandahar Cement Factory Begins Operation
item.description: The economic deputy prime minister's office announced the commencement of phase one operations at the "Shurandam" cement factory in Kandahar. The first phase has a daily capacity of 1,500 tons and will create thousands of jobs.
